rules.statement: In a test project, don't report a null-forgiving operator (`!`) that passes a deliberate null to the code under test in an argument-validation test, and don't suggest a nullable-typed helper in its place.
rules.why: The test conventions allow the null-forgiving operator in test projects for exactly this case (the project template bans it only outside them), and a nullable helper would only hide the same null.
rules.check: Before reporting `!` in test code, see whether the argument is a deliberate null passed to prove the code under test rejects it. Report it only when it suppresses a value that could instead be proven non-null, for example with a pattern match or Assert.NotNull.

rules.statement: Apply the `params IEnumerable<T>` signature convention (buffer inside the method) to test helper methods as well as production code, rather than declaring `params T[]`.
rules.why: The maintainer applied the convention to test helpers and changed `params T[]` helpers to `params IEnumerable<T>` that buffer inside, so the convention isn't limited to production code.
rules.check: Look for new or changed test helper methods that declare a `params` array parameter where `params IEnumerable<T>` would work.
